clue.text: Being with younger crowd, one may learn something

definitions.text: Being with younger crowd, one may learn something

parts.words: Being with younger crowd, one may learn something
parts.note: describes an older person who goes back to college among classmates far younger, there to study

explanation.surface: A remark that hanging around with young people can teach you a thing or two.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests picking up wisdom from youngsters; the cryptic reading is an older adult enrolled on a course alongside teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description of an adult learner studying at college or university among much younger classmates.

clue.text: Office dealing with match fixtures

parts.note: a match here is a pairing of two people and the fixtures are weddings, not sporting events

explanation.surface: Sounds like the administrative office of a sports league that arranges game schedules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match fixtures' suggests football; the match is a romantic pairing and the office is an agency that introduces people hoping to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction agency arranging partnerships between people looking for a spouse is jokingly an office fixing matches.

clue.text: Matches set up around the street

indicators.note: the reversed letters go around the abbreviation, splitting to enclose it
in a down clue, set up means the word set is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sports fixtures arranged around a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like the verb of the surface; 'up' turns it round in this down clue and 'around' makes it enclose the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Test matches are international cricket games, so tests are matches.

clue.text: What some physics is about — puzzling yet trivial

indicators.note: puzzling describes letters thrown into confusion, here the letters of yet trivial

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a branch of physics as baffling yet simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puzzling' rearranges the ten letters of YET TRIVIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's theories of special and general relativity are a major subject of modern physics.

clue.text: Galley item for ship?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a kitchen gadget on board could stand for the vessel itself.
explanation.walkthrough: A galley is a ship's kitchen, so 'galley item' pulls the solver to sea; the first sense is a cooking pan for vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking vessel that cooks food with vapour is one; so is a vessel driven by boilers, a steamship.

clue.text: One in 16 not yet established

annotationWithheld.why: One in 16 not yet established: 16 is TURNED OUT, and its word OUT is the anagram indicator for TURNED while the cross-reference supplies the fodder, so one clue reference does two jobs

clue.text: Girl sent up in programmes

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the run of letters is read upwards, backwards
in signals letters sitting inside the word programmes

explanation.surface: A girl mocked on television shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes AMME from inside 'programmes', and 'sent up' turns it round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, as in Jane Austen's heroine.

clue.text: Stop and meet train having travelled around

indicators.note: the letters of meet train move about as if on a journey, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Halt and catch a train that has gone on a circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having travelled around' rearranges the nine letters of MEET TRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something or bring it to a close is to halt it.

clue.text: Vehicle with many of its wheels immobile

definitions.text: Vehicle with many of its wheels immobile

parts.words: Vehicle with many of its wheels immobile
parts.note: the wheels belong to the cargo of autos being carried, which sit still while the lorry moves

explanation.surface: A puzzling lorry most of whose wheels never turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The stationary wheels belong to the cars stacked on the lorry's decks, not to the lorry itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A large lorry that carries several cars on its decks, whose own wheels stay still in transit.

clue.text: Rest in home, rest outside to be flexible

indicators.note: the second rest is written around the rest of the build

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the rest synonym inside the word for home

parts.note: IN means at home
to rest is to lie down

explanation.surface: Advice that resting at home, then resting outdoors, keeps you supple.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'rest' plays two parts: the first is a synonym, the second is taken as written and wraps the rest of the build. IN for 'home' is the idiom 'staying in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy that bounces back into shape is pliant and supple.

clue.text: Maiden associated with song

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A young woman famous for singing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a girl known through song, like the heroine of West Side Story's 'Maria' or the singing novice of The Sound of Music.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name celebrated in songs, such as Bernstein's 'Maria' and the singing nun-to-be of The Sound of Music.

clue.text: Little picture showing the people who think they matter?

definitions.text: the people who think they matter?

explanation.surface: A small image showing the self-important elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as two words, the fashionable clique.
explanation.definitionFit: A small illustration set within a larger one; also the in-crowd, a fashionable clique full of self-importance.

clue.text: No woman is said to be suitable for this post

indicators.note: is said signals that the word is heard rather than read, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone who is no woman is a man, a male

explanation.surface: A job advertisement suggesting only a man need apply.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at sex discrimination in hiring; 'post' is letters, not a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters and parcels delivered by the postal service.

clue.text: Puncher is seen in newspaper

indicators.note: seen in places the word is inside the abbreviation for the paper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A boxer appearing in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, the pink British business paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand is what delivers a punch.

clue.text: Well done food containing vitamins is

explanation.surface: Praise for cooking meat thoroughly, then a remark that vitamin-rich food is something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like a steak order; it is an exclamation of praise.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation congratulating someone; also wholesome, as nutritious food is healthy.

clue.text: Recovered from journey, having taken time with six deliveries

parts.note: a go can be a trip or journey
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: A traveller gets over the trip after watching some cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six balls bowled by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To get past an illness or setback is to recuperate from it.

clue.text: Happened to be evicted

explanation.surface: Someone happened to be thrown out of their home.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that came to pass, as in it proved so; also thrown out of a home.

clue.text: Picture of a mother displayed by designer

parts.note: Christian Dior was a French fashion designer
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A portrait of a woman with her mother shown by a fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed by' puts the designer's name before A and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional model scene, a kind of display picture.

clue.text: Be thought highly of or censured?

explanation.surface: Asking whether one is admired or rebuked.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words, be rated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be well rated is to be esteemed; reprimanded harshly is to have been scolded.

clue.text: Tenets coming from brute, master leading an army

parts.note: a dog is a brute beast
MA is a Master of Arts degree
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former reserve force

explanation.surface: Beliefs drawn from a beast and its master commanding troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogmata is a plural of dogma, principles laid down as beyond dispute.

clue.text: Each of them may want the lot

definitions.text: Each of them may want the lot

parts.words: Each of them may want the lot
parts.note: the lot is an item at an auction, not everything, so these people want the item under the hammer

explanation.surface: Greedy people who want everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lot' suggests everything; at an auction a lot is a single item up for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: People making offers at an auction each hope to secure the item being sold.

clue.text: Support needed at home when educationist gets job

parts.note: a BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A teacher landing employment needs help at home.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd is the British Bachelor of Education degree, held by many teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright at the corner of a bed frame holds up the bed in a house.

clue.text: Grass seen as river runs around

indicators.note: around turns the river and runs, reading them backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A plant seen when the river flows around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns DEE plus R into REED; the Dee is a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall plants growing at the water's edge belong to the grass family.

clue.text: Old silver presented to journalist

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An antique silver gift handed to a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people have grown old.

clue.text: Not an indoor celebration needed for eclipse

parts.note: something not indoor is out
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: An outdoor party is required to watch the solar eclipse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipse' is a verb, to surpass, not a solar event.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to surpass or beat them.

clue.text: The last thing one might expect to hear?

definitions.text: The last thing one might expect to hear?

parts.words: The last thing one might expect to hear?
parts.note: refers to the final horn call foretold in scripture for Judgement Day, the end of the world

explanation.surface: Something utterly surprising to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last thing one might expect' seems to mean a surprise; it is the Last Trump of the Bible, the horn blast heralding the Day of Judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Trump is the trumpet sounding on Judgement Day, the final sound anyone expects.

clue.text: A name — name given to English queen

parts.note: N again for name
N again for name

explanation.surface: A name given to an English monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Anne reigned in England and Britain from 1702 to 1714.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne was a British monarch, the last of the Stuarts.

clue.text: Fuss to get navy ornament

parts.note: ado means fuss or bother
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Making a fuss to obtain a naval decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornament' is a verb here, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate something is to embellish it.

clue.text: She tries to solve some of the newspaper industry's problems

definitions.text: She tries to solve some of the newspaper industry's problems

parts.words: She tries to solve some of the newspaper industry's problems
parts.note: the problems are readers' personal troubles sent to a paper's advice column, not the industry's commercial woes

explanation.surface: A woman trying to fix the press's business difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: The problems are not the trade's own; they are letters from readers seeking help with personal worries.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist who answers readers' letters about personal troubles in a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Psalter she put out for religious event

indicators.note: out signals the letters of psalter, she and put are disordered

explanation.surface: A woman sets aside her hymn book for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the thirteen letters of PSALTER SHE PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Christ's final meal with the apostles before the crucifixion, commemorated in the Eucharist.
